# Figure legend (generated by scripts/8_audit/h38_febio_agreement_fig.py, 2026-11-05T18:03:18)

**Fig. | Agreement of the simulation platform with FEBio holds for tied-contact cage metrics and element-level physics, but not for real-friction cage slip, and the in-house solver gpufe has no cage-level result.**

**a**, Tied-contact cage metrics from runs whose case.feb and restart.feb are byte-identical, one with the Pardiso CPU linear solver and one with the cuDSS GPU linear solver (FEBio 4.13 + patches); 15 windows in which both runs completed and reached the target moment. Orange circles: 2 windows where only the GPU run completed, excluded from the test and shown. A further 4 windows reached the target in neither run.
**b**, Horizontal cage translation under real friction (mu 0.35) at the evaluation point, for pairs of runs with byte-identical inputs. 15 pairs, 3 of which fall on opposite sides of the gate-4 limits. Largest separation: p077_gpu3 0.456 mm and p139_gpu3 0.637 mm.
**c**, C3 rotation against applied moment in the intact C3-C4 segment. FEBio reference line, gpufe markers. Moment reached by gpufe where it diverged: Extension 8%; Lateral bending +x 18%; Lateral bending −x 23%; Axial rotation +z 15%; Axial rotation −z 6%. Flexion, the only direction that finishes, has no facet contact (FEBio facet force 0 N). Directions rerun on 2026-11-05 at the time of generation: Flexion, Extension, Axial rotation −z; other directions show the last full attempt of 2026-10-28 (gpufe solver files last changed 2026-10-28 02:27).
**d**, Moment reached in each gate 2 attempt. One batch lost to a GPU driver assert is left out.
**e**, Equivalence tests. Dots are single cases (a window, direction or material), never time points, because time points within a run are not independent. Margins come only from documents that predate this analysis: NUM-10 and NUM-11 0.01%; PI 2026-11-03 numerical tolerances 2% (time step, strictest) and 5% (mesh and penalty, loosest); gate plan 1% (gate 1), 2% (gate 1c script), 5% (gate 2), 10% (gate 3).

## Statistics
- e = (platform - reference) / |reference|, or a norm-based relative error where the quantity is a field. Repeat runs have no natural reference, so they use |a - b| / mean(a, b), and for groups of three runs the largest pair.
- Test: H0 mean|e| >= margin against H1 mean|e| < margin, one-sided t test, Holm-adjusted over the 14 rows tested. Two one-sided tests reduce to this because |e| >= 0, and the test on |e| is stricter than the usual test on signed e.
- Equivalent = adjusted p < 0.05 AND every case inside the margin. Not equivalent = at least one case outside the margin.
- The simulations are deterministic in intent, so the p-values describe the spread over the tested cases, not sampling of a population. They do not extend to designs or load cases outside the tested set.
- Robustness: errors span many orders of magnitude, so the exact Wilcoxon version is in equivalence_tests.csv. It agrees on every row, except that n = 2 or 3 cannot reach p < 0.05 by construction (gate 1b, n = 3: exact p = 0.125; its maximum error is 4 orders below the margin).
- Windows of one design share an insertion. Design-level sensitivity, one value per design (3 designs), worst-window p (margin 2%): mu_sq 0.0014, slip bound 0.00058, N 2.2e-05, peak compression 0.00043.
- At the registered NUM-11 margin of 0.01%, tied metrics are not equivalent: windows above it are {'mu': 3, 'slip': 2, 'N': 2, 'peak': 2}. Maximum |e|: mu_sq 0.33%, slip bound 0.2%, N 0.043%, peak compression 0.17%, tied cage translation 0.58%.

## Limits of this figure
- Section A compares FEBio with itself under different linear solvers and builds. It shows that the platform's changes do not move tied results by more than the margins. It is not an independent validation of the FEBio model; that is the role of the PHY checks against cadaver data.
- Tied results were compared on 3 designs (p100: family A, radial interleave, d 0.80 mm; p117: family A, radial interleave, d 0.65 mm; p113: family A, radial mix, d 0.50 mm), so they do not cover the whole design space.
- Friction comparisons have few independent inputs (n = 3 GPU vs CPU, 7 GPU vs GPU). They come from physio_fric3 (density 1e-6), which is provisional; the physio_fric4 reference rerun has not replaced it.
- Gates 1b and 1c ran on the earlier dynamic-relaxation solver, not the current Newton solver (findings F-0014, F-0026). In gate 1c the gate's own 2 % criterion is against the Coulomb law, so that row uses the law: with n = 2 the test cannot conclude, though both cases are inside the margin (1.1%, 0.76%). At mu 0.5 gpufe gives 0.496 and FEBio 0.457, so the 8.6 % gap between them is FEBio's own distance from the law, not a gpufe error. FEBio is also not a valid reference for stick memory (verifier note v05).
- C0-C7 row: the PI ruled NUM-10 partial on this case (2026-11-05 06:38).
- Sliding normal force row: gate 1c reports about 2 % as an observation, no margin was ever set, so no verdict is given.

## Terms used in this legend
PI, principal investigator; QA, quality assurance; PHY, physics checks of the capability register (against cadaver and literature data); NUM-10, FEBio patch regression check; NUM-11, GPU versus CPU linear solver check; gate 1d, stick-memory benchmark of gpufe (not plotted, FEBio is not a valid reference for it).
